title: Integration of Whole-Body Skin Imaging into the Regional Healthcare Infrastructure to Ensure Comprehensive and Future-Oriented Dermatological Care in Bavaria
summary:
The project SMART REGIO DERM aims to improve dermatological care in underserved and structurally weak regions of Bavaria through the use of whole-body skin scanners. With approximately 30% of the population affected by skin diseases, the project addresses a substantial need for efficient and accessible dermatological care.

The high-resolution 3D whole-body scans are analyzed teledermatologically, enabling rapid and accurate diagnostic support and facilitating effective triage and referral to appropriate treatment pathways. As a model project, the scanner is currently implemented in a general practitioner’s practice in the municipality of Ried, providing access to patients from Swabia and Upper Bavaria. In the long term, the project will integrate additional technologies such as online appointment platforms embedded within Germany’s national telematics infrastructure, further increasing efficiency and accessibility.

The overarching goal is to enhance access, diagnostic timeliness, and treatment efficiency, thereby ensuring the sustainability of comprehensive dermatological care across Bavaria. Target groups include individuals with visible skin changes as well as the general population aged 35 and older for skin cancer screening as recommended by statutory health insurance guidelines.

SMART REGIO DERM will be evaluated in a process- and outcome-oriented manner regarding its feasibility, utility, and acceptance among the population. The evaluation criteria include:

Early access to dermatological diagnosis and treatment
Improved accessibility to medical care in underserved regions
Reduced waiting times
Increased uptake of skin cancer screening
Patient satisfaction
Additionally, the project will be assessed in terms of its economic impact, with the aim of adapting it as an innovative standard of care for other regions in Bavaria lacking adequate dermatological services.
